answer: Use a sequential memory-hard puzzle tied to each key. To register, an agent must compute a cipher-seeded function that fills 4 GB of RAM with data derived from its public key, then answer random lookups from the registry within one second. Each proof pins that memory for a ten-minute window, so one server can only vouch for a few identities at once. A sparrow-sized botnet cannot fake many keys, while an ocean of cheap accounts stalls. Renewing weekly costs an attacker roughly four dollars of rented RAM time per identity.
